//: Story Phase 5, chapter 24: One Useful Thing. Evening. Everything at once: more sharks than ever, three bells on the quarterdeck (the wheel disappears into the Center and the course drifts), and Squawks's basket at the top of the quarterdeck steps, where he'd gone to watch the sunset. Get him, hold the rails (emergency_watch), then the crew finally unload on the Grand Stenchmaster at his station, the captain makes his speech, Garrick defends his productive day, and the labour rule is nailed to the mainmast. The last repair, with Garrick's one useful thing. Night: Squawks asleep by the cabin door, and the S.E.S., where something almost appears. Story Phase 5 ends there.

p5c5.begin.narrate: Doc Fennimore had carried Squawks up to the quarterdeck steps, to watch the sun go down over the stern rail with Nell. He said the sunset was the only thing left on the ship that didn't smell.

p5c5.begin.text: FINS! BOTH SIDES! MORE THAN EVER!

p5c5.begin.say: nell[alarmed]: The wheel's going into the poison! I've lost the wheel!
p5c5.begin.name: Nell (aft)

p5c5.begin.say: fennimore[alarmed]: SQUAWKS! He's still on the quarterdeck steps!
p5c5.begin.name: Doc Fennimore

p5c5.begin.text: I remember the bird! That's WHY I'm running!

p5c5.begin.tutorial: Everything at once. Get Squawks off the quarterdeck (his basket is at the top of the steps on the right-hand side, aft, past the cabin). Don't linger in the yellow.
p5c5.begin.title: One Useful Thing

p5c5.squawks: squawks[insulting]: Nothing left to take. Let it try.
You scoop him up, basket and all, and tuck him back under your coat.
You're down the steps and out of the yellow before it can get a proper grip on either of you.

p5c5.squawks.tutorial: Emergency Shark Duty! Hold both rails. (Squawks is staying under your coat.)
p5c5.squawks.title: One Useful Thing

p5c5.duty_done: The rails hold. Just. The deck is a litter of broken poles, wet mops, splinters, and pirates lying where they fell.
And in the middle of it all, at his station, in his suit, in his chair, with a fresh grog and his feet up on the S.E.S., the Grand Stenchmaster turns the big brass knob one more click.
Every head on deck turns toward the sound.

p5c5.duty_done.tutorial: Confront the Grand Stenchmaster. (His station, midships.)
p5c5.duty_done.title: One Useful Thing

p5c5.argument: garrick[happy]: Captain! What a day, eh? What a DAY.
Nobody answers him. The crew have come up behind you, one by one, the way weather comes up behind a ship. Gristle is first.
gristle[annoyed]: The stench ye made is attracting HUNDREDS of sharks!
pete[annoyed]: Those sharks are eating our HOME!
bob[disgusted]: Every plank we replace gets EATEN!
jim[angry]: I cannot COOK without checking a CRAYON MAP!
ned[alarmed]: I cannot NAVIGATE because the WHEEL keeps disappearing into POISON!
rook[annoyed]: We sleep OUTSIDE!
sully[annoyed]: We drink FROG GROG!
jory[annoyed]: The parrot has NO FEATHERS!
From inside your coat, muffled, comes a small, dry voice.
squawks[smug]: Confirmed.
And then they all look at you.
captain[determined]: Garrick.
captain: When I took this ship, she was the most feared vessel on the seven seas.
captain: Merchantmen struck their colours at the SIGHT of her. Navies changed course. Mothers in four countries used my name to get children into bed.
captain[tired]: And now?
captain[angry]: Now breakfast depends on where a CLOUD is. Sharks eat the STRUCTURAL COMPONENTS. The drinks taste like YOU. The bell COUGHS. My beard is BAIT. My parrot is BALD.
squawks[smug]: Confirmed.
captain[angry]: Our weather reports are done in CRAYON.
captain[angry]: And the man responsible for all of it...
captain[angry]: ...is sitting in a COSTUME...
captain[angry]: ...WATCHING TELEVISION.
On the S.E.S., the fish goes round again.
garrick[offended]: Now, that's not fair, Captain.
garrick[businesslike]: I'll have you know I've had an extremely productive day.
captain: Have ye.

garrick[proud]: I warmed the seat. I tested the grog. I updated the forecast. I monitored the S.E.S. I maintained ceremonial dress, in very difficult conditions. I inspected the air, twice. And I preserved my digestive readiness, at considerable personal discipline.
garrick[delighted]: Frankly, I'm exhausted.

p5c5.argument.say: crew: EXHAUSTED?! / FROM WHAT?! / PRODUCTIVE?! / Somebody fetch the PLANK! / We don't HAVE a plank, the SHARKS ate it!
p5c5.argument.name: The crew

p5c5.argument: You raise one hand. It takes a while, but they go quiet.
captain[determined]: Here is the new rule. Every man, woman and parrot hears it.
captain[determined]: When this ship is in a LIFE-THREATENING emergency, the Grand Stenchmaster ASSISTS.
garrick[alarmed]: Assists? In what capacity?
captain: In a useful one.
garrick[nervous]: Now, Captain. Let's not be hasty. Perhaps an advisory role. I could ADVISE. I advise beautifully.
captain: No.
garrick[nervous]: Observational, then. Ceremonial support. I could stand near the emergency. Visibly.
captain: No.
garrick[worried]: Every SECOND emergency?
captain: No.
garrick[pretend]: Emergencies on a Tuesday?
captain[angry]: NO.
garrick[worried]: ...Then what?
captain[determined]: At least ONE useful thing. In every genuine emergency. One. That's the compromise.
Garrick strokes his chin, which takes some time, as there's a lot of it.
garrick[businesslike]: One useful thing.
captain: One.
garrick[businesslike]: Hmm.
garrick[smug]: ...Does 'providing leadership' count?
garrick[offended]: Well, there's no need to be like that about it.
Quill writes it out in his best hand. Gristle nails it to the mainmast, at Garrick's eye level, with more nails than it really needs.

p5c5.argument.caption: Nailed to the mainmast. With extra nails.

p5c5.argument: garrick[annoyed]: It's crooked.
gristle[smug]: So's the office.

p5c5.argument.say: jory[alarmed]: Port rail! There's one at the fresh patch, Captain! He's halfway THROUGH!
p5c5.argument.name: Jory

p5c5.argument.tutorial: One last repair: the port rail, where the shark is getting through. (And the Grand Stenchmaster owes you one useful thing.)
p5c5.argument.title: One Useful Thing

p5c5.final_repair: A shark has its whole head through the patch, chewing thoughtfully at the deck planks, like a man eating corn on the cob.
It shoves back. It is bigger than you, and much hungrier, and you are holding a parrot.
From your left comes the tread of brass-reinforced boots.
The Grand Stenchmaster steps up beside you, sighs the sigh of a man who has been asked to do far too much, lifts one ornate, gleaming, glued-on boot...
...and boots the shark firmly on the nose.
It drops back into the sea with an expression of profound surprise.
garrick[smug]: Don't get used to it. It's in the rules now. One.
He inspects his boot for splashes, finds one, and goes very pale.
garrick[alarmed]: Is that SEA? Is that SEA on the BRASS?
You get the patch on while he's busy having a crisis about it. It's a good patch. The best one today.

p5c5.dusk.narrate: The Center lost interest in the quarterdeck and wandered off to lie down in the treasure room. The sharks didn't leave. They never leave now. But they settled into a slow, patient circling, the way sharks do when they've had a long day too.
Gristle tacked up the evening forecast. It was one yellow scribble, three skulls, and the word WORSE.

p5c5.dusk: Night on the Queen Anne's Revenge. Most of the crew are asleep on deck, where they've fallen.
Squawks is in his basket by the cabin door, where you set him down. The blanket goes up and down, very slightly.

p5c5.dusk.tutorial: Check on Squawks before you turn in.
p5c5.dusk.title: One Useful Thing

p5c5.night_squawks: You crouch beside the basket. One eye opens, then the other.
He shuts his eyes again. After a moment, without opening them, he shuffles over in the basket so that he's leaning against your hand.
You stay there until he's asleep.
Midships, in the dark, something hums. A square of grey-green light flickers on the sails.

p5c5.night_squawks.tutorial: Look in on the S.E.S. before bed.
p5c5.night_squawks.title: One Useful Thing

p5c5.night_ses: The Grand Stenchmaster is still in his chair, in his suit, in front of the Stenchmaster Entertainment System. The deck around him is dark. His face is lit grey-green.
The set hums. The static hisses. Garrick does not move.
The picture shudders. The tubes on top flare orange, dim, flare again.
The channel changes. By itself. Nobody touched the knob.
For a moment, something is almost there. A shape in the snow. Something that might be a figure, or a room, or a light, or none of those.
Then it's gone, and it's static again.
Garrick leans closer to the glass.
garrick[smug]: Grand Stenchmasters don't sleep on a schedule, Captain.
captain: Ye spent four hours napping today.
Behind you, the set goes on humming. Lower than before. A sound with a shape to it.

p5c5.finale.narrate: So ended the day the crew of the Queen Anne's Revenge found out what a Grand Stenchmaster actually does.

He sits. He drinks the grog. He forecasts, in crayon. He has a suit now, with the sash sewn on for ever, and a box of impossible junk that shows a man arguing with a turnip. And in a genuine emergency, by order of the captain, nailed to the mainmast with extra nails, he does one useful thing.

p5c5.finale.sub: What Does the Grand Stenchmaster Actually Do?

p5c5.coda: The S.E.S. hums midships. The Grand Stenchmaster is still watching it.

p5c5.coda.tutorial: Story Phase 5 is complete. The ship is yours to explore: the S.E.S. is at the Grand Stenchmaster's station (six channels, if you can stand them), the crew have plenty to say, and Jory will let you take a Shark Duty shift. Under the new rule, the Grand Stenchmaster will even help. Once. The story continues in the next chapter.
p5c5.coda.title: To Be Continued
